MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MARCH 6, 2023

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR YOO at 7:05 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar, Friedman

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, FEBRUARY 6, 2023

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 6,
  2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE TO IMPLEMENT THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES GENERAL
  PLAN

Community Development Director Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff
report. She stated that there are no major changes in the residential districts; there will be clean-
up and removal of obsolete Zoning Chapters, which include the Quarry District and the Research
and Scientific District; and adoption of the new Zoning Map to be consistent with the General
Plan. Staff will be focusing on the Commercial District; the new Commercial District Mixed-Use
Overlay Zone; and the new Institutional Workforce Housing Overlay District.

Director Naughton explained the difference between a Form-Based and Euclidean or Traditional
Zoning Code and stated that a hybrid approach may work best for the City. She also provided an
overview of changes to the Commercial District.

Director Naughton stated that this will take approximately 12-16 months to complete, and priority
will be on the Commercial District and the creation of the new Overlay Districts.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if there are any new uses considered in the Commercial
District. Director Naughton responded that an example is that housing will be permitted by right,

  1
 which is a reason that it is important to incorporate all the aspects that are considered in a
discretionary process and build them into the code. There will be a focus on flex-commercial
space; however, uses are important and need to be reviewed for noise and other factors.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked for clarification on what would be defined as an extraordinary
benefit to the community regarding bonus density housing. Director Naughton stated that City
Council Resolution No. 2531 lists what the City Council has defined as a community benefit.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if the City Council would give final approval of the concessions
for the Density Bonus Program. Director Naughton stated that it would through the development
agreement process.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if these can include compensation paid by the developer.
Director Naughton stated that the preference would be for the proposed benefit to be implemented
rather than taking a fee; the City would need to take the fee and place it in a trust account to be
built at a later date where there is risk that the cost to make the improvement will increase.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if a developer can make improvements off-site for the
benefit of the City and get increased density. Director Naughton stated that this is correct.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if these are State imposed things that the City is
implementing. Director Naughton stated that the market study showed that the City has a high
land value, and it’s difficult for a developer to incorporate, for example, affordable housing; this is
a way to incentivize projects by offering higher density in exchange for community benefits.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the high density numbers are imposed or required by
the State. Director Naughton stated that the State is not requiring any specific density; however,
cities are required to plan for a certain amount of housing within the next eight years.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked how much consideration is being given to traffic in the City.
Director Naughton stated that as part of the General Plan there was an Environmental Impact
Report prepared and it included transportation; traffic impacts; and vehicle miles traveled (VMT)
analysis. The traffic impact analysis looked at a 20-year build out of the entire City.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about the deadline for the certification of the Housing Element.
Director Naughton stated that in June of 2022, there was an extension given to cities that needed
to rezone in order to be certified. HCD staff informed the City that it was low priority, in light of
cities that required the extension.staff submitted the draft Housing Element in the Fall informally
and again in the Winter, formally. In early February, HCD informed the City that not only had it
not addressed all the comments, but there were also programmatic and policy changes required.
Staff is working with HCD to address all the issues and get it certified.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about a Times article on the developer’s remedy. Director
Naughton stated that any jurisdiction that does not have a certified housing element can be
subject to an application under the builder’s remedy provision. It allows for developers to apply
for a project that doesn’t adhere to the zoning or general plan designation as long as 20% of the
project is affordable housing but it is still subject to review under CEQA.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked how a developer would be prevented from going above the
maximum height. Director Naughton stated that if the maximum height is set in the code and a
project wanted a building height beyond what the code allows, an applicant would need to apply
for a Variance, which would be a discretionary review.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about the reason for adding more detail to the Zoning
Code. Director Naughton stated that there is a need to change to less reliance on discretionary
reviews to a “by right” type of process and there is a need to provide more information upfront.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI expressed his concern with checks and balances with the
Planning Commission and/or staff, and making sure to clarify any gray areas prior to proceeding
with a project.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that it seems that there is going to be an increase in density in
the Commercial District and asked if there has been feedback from the utility companies, public
works, fire department, etc. and how they will allow for this increase and the impact to the General
Plan. Director Naughton stated that all these departments were included in the discussion and
preparation of the General Plan. The infrastructure is in place to accommodate the increased
density.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if a project meets the new requirements, then there is no

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 6, 2023
  2
 Planning Commission review. Director Naughton confirmed this and stated that projects are still
subject to review under CEQA. The City is in a difficult position due to VMT and the hope is that
projects will be able to rely on the General Plan EIR and tier off the environmental review. There
will be a requirement for a Traffic Impact Analysis for projects that require a development
agreement.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE THIS UPDATE.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

COMMISSIONER OLSON commented that he appreciates the work that staff has done.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386; LOCATION: 39 Empty Saddle Road;
  APPLICANT: Michael Hasegawa (on behalf of Verizon Wireless); A request for a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP-220387) for a new stealth telecommunication facility
  featuring a 64’-high monoeucalyptus structure located toward the rear of the property
  including 17 antennas (8 panel antennas, 4 CBRS antennas, 4 C-Band antennas, and 1
  microwave antenna) and 16 wireless radios on 4 arrays, a 342 square-foot lease area that
  features 3 equipment cabinets, 1 generator and will be fully enclosed with an 8’-high CMU
  wall.

Director Naughton stated that this item is being recommended to be continued to the Planning
Commission meeting of April 3, 2023. The applicant is organizing a community meeting and staff
will not be part of that meeting. Staff encouraged Verizon to hold a community meeting prior to
coming before the Planning Commission due to the amount of comments received. Staff will be
reaching out to the applicant and make sure to post information on the meeting on the City’s
website. Staff will also be contacting those who provided public comment regarding the new April
3 Public Hearing date. Public notice will be published in the paper and notices will be sent to a
500’ radius from the project site.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER
to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386 TO THE APRIL 3, 2023
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

AYES: Yoo, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar, Friedman
ABSTAIN:

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

NONE

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the SBCCOG General Assembly. Director Naughton
stated that the event is on March 23 and the topic is sustainability and resiliency; some of the
City’s initiatives will be featured at the event.

12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, FEBRUARY 14, 2023

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

13.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR YOO adjourned the meeting at 8:05 p.m.
